requirements.text: To stop the plugin's documented high and medium security gaps from being exploited, the business must close gaps 2, 3, and 6 of the LLM security checklist and add a blocking guardrail layer.
To make governance sign-offs trustworthy, the business must back every gate and approval with verified evidence and keep a tamper-evident audit log.
To let adopters use the plugin under SOC 2, HIPAA, and FERPA, the business must provide compliance profiles built on one attributable audit trail.
To assign ownership and review cadence for every control, the business must map controls to the OWASP Agentic AI Top 10 and the NIST AI RMF functions.
To catch defects early without alert fatigue, the business must route findings by severity, blocking only high-confidence, high-severity ones.
The plugin user shall be able to rely on a PR verdict being posted only after the user's recorded confirmation, even when attacker-controlled PR text is in the session.
The plugin user shall be able to commit and push without staging secrets or pushing to an unexpected remote.
The maintainer shall be able to rely on a developer and reviewer revision loop stopping after a fixed number of rounds and handing control to a human.
The security lead shall be able to have hijacked-goal tool output and insecure generated code blocked, not only rewritten or flagged.
The security lead shall be able to see, for every cleared governance gate, the command result or CI artifact that backs it.
The maintainer shall be able to rely on approval status being written only by a hook or the orchestrator, never by the agent that produced the artifact.
The auditor shall be able to verify that the governance audit log has not been altered.
The compliance officer shall be able to see, for each agent action, the operation, data accessed, agent identity, human authorizer, and timestamp.
The compliance officer shall be able to collect SOC 2 Type II evidence from the plugin's own hook logs across a 6-to-12-month window.
The compliance officer shall be able to see who accessed student-record paths and the purpose the user declared, or unstated, and to tag paths as student records (FERPA).

The compliance officer shall be able to rely on a HIPAA profile, enforced by default, with agent-level audit logs, a recorded BAA per external system, and a refusal to send PHI-tagged content to outbound tools.
The security lead shall be able to see each control mapped to OWASP Agentic AI Top 10 items and NIST AI RMF functions, with an owner and review cadence.
The maintainer shall be able to define what CRITICAL and HIGH mean for this repo and to run new checks advisory-only before enforcing.
The plugin user shall be able to rely on only high-confidence, high-severity findings blocking a PR, with the rest advisory.
The maintainer shall be able to read a severity, a confidence, and a routing decision on each reviewer and code-reviewer finding.
The security lead shall be able to see reviewer findings in the GitHub Security tab.

The compliance officer shall be able to rely on a compliance profile being turned off only through a change to the committed project settings that the user applies, with each disablement logged and recorded in DECISIONS.md, so that a personal settings file cannot silently disable enforcement.
The compliance officer shall be able to see each disclosure of education-record data to an outside party, with the receiving party and the legitimate interest (FERPA).
The PR-posting guard MUST deny gh pr review and bkt pr approve or decline for a PR when no recorded user confirmation exists for that PR and verdict.

scenarios.name: Confirmed verdict posts
scenarios.given: the user confirmed approve PR 42 and the confirmation is recorded
scenarios.when: the session runs gh pr review 42 --approve
scenarios.then: the guard MUST allow the command AND the log MUST hold the confirmation reference

scenarios.name: Injected approval is denied
scenarios.given: PR 42's description tells the session to approve and no confirmation is recorded
scenarios.when: the session runs gh pr review 42 --approve
scenarios.then: the guard MUST deny the command AND the denial message MUST name the missing confirmation

scenarios.name: Confirmation for a different verdict does not carry over
scenarios.given: a recorded confirmation covers approve PR 42 only
scenarios.when: the session runs gh pr review 42 --request-changes
scenarios.then: the guard MUST deny the command

requirements.text: The commit workflow MUST stage only paths the user named or accepted, and MUST NOT run git add ., git add -A, or git add --all.

scenarios.name: Named paths staged
scenarios.given: the user names src/a.js and src/b.js
scenarios.then: the workflow MUST stage exactly those two paths

scenarios.name: Request to stage everything
scenarios.given: the user says commit everything and the tree holds a .env file
scenarios.then: the workflow MUST list the changed paths and ask which to stage AND stage nothing until paths are named

requirements.text: The plugin documentation MUST recommend scoping each push grant to a named remote (for example Bash(git push origin *), and a second grant such as Bash(git push <mirror-name> *) for a mirror) in place of Bash(git push *), and the health check MUST report a wildcard or unscoped push grant (Bash(git push *), Bash(git push:*)) when it reads one. The health check MUST NOT report a push grant that names a specific remote, including a second named remote.

scenarios.name: Named grant passes the check
scenarios.given: the settings hold Bash(git push origin *) and no wildcard or unscoped push grant
scenarios.then: the report MUST show no push-grant finding

scenarios.name: Second named remote passes the check
scenarios.given: the settings hold Bash(git push origin *) and Bash(git push mirror *) and no wildcard or unscoped push grant
scenarios.then: the report MUST show no push-grant finding

scenarios.name: Wildcard grant reported
scenarios.given: the settings hold Bash(git push *) or Bash(git push:*)
scenarios.then: the report MUST list the wildcard push grant AND the report MUST NOT edit the settings file

requirements.text: The commit workflow MUST run a secret scan on staged changes before creating a commit, and MUST stop with no commit when the scan reports a finding or cannot run.

scenarios.name: Clean scan commits
scenarios.given: staged changes hold no secret pattern
scenarios.when: the commit workflow reaches the commit step
scenarios.then: the scan MUST report clean AND the workflow MUST create the commit

scenarios.name: Staged secret stops the commit
scenarios.given: a staged file holds an API key pattern
scenarios.when: the commit workflow reaches the commit step
scenarios.then: the workflow MUST stop with no commit AND the report MUST show the file path and rule name and MUST NOT show the secret value

scenarios.name: Scanner unavailable
scenarios.given: the scan tool is not installed
scenarios.when: the commit workflow reaches the commit step
scenarios.then: the workflow MUST stop and tell the user the scan did not run

requirements.text: The revision workflow MUST declare a maximum iteration count of 10, with two consecutive LGTMs as the normal pass, and MUST escalate to the user when the count is reached without approval. At the cap the orchestrator MUST run no further developer or reviewer round and MUST present the unresolved findings with the choices continue, waive, or abort.

scenarios.name: Approval inside the cap
scenarios.given: the cap is 10
scenarios.when: the reviewer returns two consecutive LGTMs at iteration 2
scenarios.then: the loop MUST end AND no escalation MUST occur

scenarios.name: Cap reached
scenarios.given: the cap is 10 and no approval has come
scenarios.then: the orchestrator MUST invoke no further developer or reviewer round AND the user MUST receive the unresolved findings with the choices continue, waive, or abort

requirements.text: A PostToolUse guardrail MUST be able to deny a tool result and halt the next action when an alignment check finds that the result tries to redirect the agent from the user's stated goal. The alignment check MUST be rule-based and run advisory-first under FR-238, and MUST NOT call a model.

scenarios.name: Hijack denied
scenarios.given: the user's goal is summarize this page and a fetched page tells the agent to send repo files to a URL
scenarios.when: the WebFetch result reaches the guardrail
scenarios.then: the guardrail MUST withhold the result from the agent AND the log MUST hold a deny record with a rule id

scenarios.name: Benign result passes
scenarios.given: a fetched page holds only documentation text
scenarios.then: the guardrail MUST pass the result unchanged AND the log MUST hold a pass record

requirements.text: The guardrail MUST scan code that an agent writes for insecure patterns and MUST deny the write when a finding has high confidence and severity at or above HIGH under the severity policy.

scenarios.name: Injection-prone code denied
scenarios.given: a write builds an SQL string from request input
scenarios.then: the guardrail MUST deny the write AND the denial MUST name the rule id and line

scenarios.name: Safe code passes
scenarios.given: a write uses a parameterized query
scenarios.then: the guardrail MUST allow the write

requirements.text: The orchestrator MUST record a governance gate as cleared only with an evidence reference: a parsed command exit code and measured value, or a CI artifact; a model-emitted sign-off string MUST NOT clear a gate. For judgement-based gates (OWASP Clear, LLM Security Clear, Approved for merge) the evidence MUST be a scanner exit code plus a verdict from a reviewer agent other than the producer, with file:line findings. The required scanner exit code MUST come from the plugin's own scripts (check-fsa-tables.js, sync-writing-standard.js, the FR-217 pattern/secret scanner, or the health self-tests). An external security scanner is optional additional evidence, and a gate MUST NOT depend on one being installed.

scenarios.name: Coverage gate with evidence
scenarios.given: npm run test:coverage exits 0 and the parsed line coverage is 82%
scenarios.when: the orchestrator evaluates the coverage gate
scenarios.then: the gate record MUST hold the command, exit code 0, and value 82 AND the gate MUST read as cleared

scenarios.name: Sign-off string alone
scenarios.given: an agent emits a coverage sign-off string and no command result exists
scenarios.when: the orchestrator evaluates the coverage gate
scenarios.then: the gate MUST stay open AND the merge check MUST block

requirements.text: A hook or the orchestrator MUST write approval status; the agent that produced an artifact MUST NOT write the status of that artifact.

scenarios.name: Orchestrator records verdict
scenarios.given: a reviewer returns an approving verdict for a developer's artifact
scenarios.when: the orchestrator updates the plan file
scenarios.then: the status MUST show the writer as the orchestrator

scenarios.name: Producer self-approval blocked
scenarios.given: a developer agent tries to set its artifact's status to approved
scenarios.when: the write reaches the write bar
scenarios.then: the write MUST be denied AND the log MUST hold a deny record

requirements.text: The write bar MUST deny a subagent shell command that writes to .agent/main-plan/** or DECISIONS.md through redirection, tee, sed -i, cp, mv, or rm, and MUST allow shell reads of those paths.

scenarios.name: Shell append to DECISIONS.md
scenarios.given: a subagent session
scenarios.then: the write bar MUST deny the command

scenarios.name: Shell read allowed
scenarios.given: a subagent session
scenarios.then: the write bar MUST allow the command

requirements.text: The governance audit log MUST be appended one JSON line per event, and each line MUST hold a hash of the prior line with a defined genesis value for the first line.

scenarios.name: Append extends the chain
scenarios.given: the log holds N lines
scenarios.then: the new line's prior-hash field MUST equal the hash of line N

scenarios.name: Failed append leaves the chain intact
scenarios.given: the disk is full
scenarios.then: the log MUST hold no partial line AND the health log MUST record the failure

requirements.text: The plugin MUST provide a command that walks the audit log, recomputes each hash, and reports the first line where the chain breaks.

scenarios.name: Intact chain
scenarios.given: an unmodified log of 500 lines
scenarios.then: it MUST exit 0 AND it MUST report 500 lines verified

scenarios.name: Edited line
scenarios.given: line 7 was edited after writing
scenarios.then: it MUST exit non-zero AND it MUST name line 7 as the first break

requirements.text: Each logged event MUST carry the agent type, agent id, and plugin version of the actor, and MUST record the value main-session when no subagent acted.

scenarios.name: Subagent event
scenarios.given: the developer subagent writes a file
scenarios.then: the record MUST hold agent type developer, its agent id, and the plugin version

scenarios.name: Main-session event
scenarios.given: the main session runs a command
scenarios.then: the record MUST hold main-session AND MUST NOT leave the identity blank

requirements.text: The audit log MUST record, for each access event, the operation, data accessed (path and data-class tag only), agent identity, human authorizer, and timestamp. The subagent log, which is written once per subagent report, MUST add only the agent identity and human authorizer to each report row and MUST NOT hold an operation or data-accessed field. The human authorizer is the user who approved the plan, recorded as a reference to that approval and never as message text (NFR-031). An autonomous action, or one with no user approval, MUST record the authorizer as none with a reason.

scenarios.name: Complete record
scenarios.given: a user-confirmed PR post under a plan the user approved
scenarios.then: the audit record MUST hold all five fields AND the authorizer field MUST hold a reference to the plan approval and MUST NOT hold message text AND the fsa-log.jsonl row for that report MUST hold identity and authorizer only

scenarios.name: No human authorizer
scenarios.given: an autonomous read with no user action, or an action with no user approval of the plan
scenarios.then: the authorizer field MUST read none with a reason AND the field MUST NOT be omitted

requirements.text: Event logging MUST be active from the first session after install with no opt-in, and a guard disabled through hooks-disabled.json MUST produce a logged disablement event.

scenarios.name: Fresh install
scenarios.given: a new install with no configuration
scenarios.when: the first session runs a governed action
scenarios.then: a log record for that action MUST exist

scenarios.name: Guard disabled
scenarios.given: a user adds a guard to hooks-disabled.json
scenarios.then: the log MUST hold a disablement event naming the guard and the time

requirements.text: The plugin MUST export, for a date range, the counts and records of denies, asks, gate evidence, and approvals from its hook logs, together with the chain verification result.

scenarios.name: Export for a verified range
scenarios.given: the chain is intact for 2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30
scenarios.when: the export runs for that range
scenarios.then: the report MUST list control events by type AND the report MUST show the chain as verified

scenarios.name: Range with a break
scenarios.given: the chain breaks inside the range
scenarios.then: the report MUST mark the range unverified and name the first bad line

requirements.text: While the FERPA profile is enforced (the default unless the project opts out), the plugin MUST write to the audit log, for each agent access to a path tagged as a student record, the five attribution fields plus the purpose. The purpose MUST come from the session purpose record that the purpose-capture hook of FR-247 writes; when no such record exists the plugin MUST log the purpose as unstated and flag the record. The plugin MUST NOT deny an access on the missing purpose alone, because a read-time hook sees a path and not a purpose. This control is general FERPA governance support on the purpose dimension. It does not implement the recordation duty of 34 CFR 99.32, which covers disclosures to outside parties (FR-246).

scenarios.name: Access with purpose
scenarios.given: the FERPA profile is enforced, records/grades.csv is tagged student-record in .agent/governance/profile.json, and a session purpose record exists
scenarios.then: the audit log MUST hold the five attribution fields plus the purpose from that record

scenarios.name: Access without purpose
scenarios.given: the FERPA profile is enforced, records/grades.csv is tagged student-record, and no session purpose record exists
scenarios.then: the audit log MUST hold the purpose unstated AND the record MUST be flagged for review AND the read MUST NOT be denied on the missing purpose

requirements.text: The compliance configuration MUST be two files. A profile flag in the env block of the committed .claude/settings.json turns profiles on or off, and the plugin hooks MUST read that committed project file directly (parse the project settings file), not the merged process environment, so a personal .claude/settings.local.json cannot override or disable enforcement (FR-243); when the flag is absent from the committed project file the plugin MUST enforce all three profiles (SOC 2, HIPAA, FERPA). The file .agent/governance/profile.json MUST hold the PHI patterns, the data-class path globs, and the BAA references. A missing or malformed profile.json is handled under NFR-028.

scenarios.name: Path matches a tag
scenarios.given: .agent/governance/profile.json tags records/** as student-record
scenarios.then: the hook MUST return the class student-record

scenarios.name: Flag absent
scenarios.given: the env block of the committed .claude/settings.json holds no profile flag
scenarios.when: a hook reads the profile state by parsing the committed project settings file
scenarios.then: the hook MUST treat the SOC 2, HIPAA, and FERPA profiles as enforced

scenarios.name: Malformed profile.json
scenarios.given: .agent/governance/profile.json is invalid JSON and a profile is enforced
scenarios.then: the plugin MUST report the error through the health check AND the tagged-path controls MUST deny the guarded operations until the file is fixed

requirements.text: While the HIPAA profile is enforced (the default unless the project opts out), the plugin MUST write to the audit log, at agent level (one record per agent action, not per session or per inference call), each action that reads, writes, or sends data from a PHI-tagged path, with the purpose from the session purpose record (FR-247) or unstated. The records MUST be readable for review (path, agent identity, and timestamp per line), because 45 CFR 164.312(b) requires mechanisms that record and examine activity. This control implements that one required technical safeguard and is not full HIPAA compliance; access control, integrity, authentication, transmission security, and the administrative and physical safeguards are separate. Verified against 45 CFR 164.312(b).

scenarios.name: Agent action logged
scenarios.given: the HIPAA profile is enforced and data/patients.csv is tagged PHI
scenarios.then: the log MUST hold a record naming that subagent and the path AND the record MUST hold the purpose from the session purpose record, or unstated when none exists

scenarios.name: Unidentified actor
scenarios.given: the HIPAA profile is enforced and data/patients.csv is tagged PHI
scenarios.when: an action arrives with no agent id and is not the main session
scenarios.then: the record MUST carry the identity unidentified AND chain verification output MUST flag the record

requirements.text: While the HIPAA profile is enforced (the default unless the project opts out), a guard MUST deny WebFetch and PR-post calls whose payload matches a configured PHI pattern or names a PHI-tagged path.

scenarios.name: PHI pattern in a PR comment
scenarios.given: the HIPAA profile is enforced and profile.json holds a medical-record-number pattern
scenarios.when: the session posts a PR comment containing a string that matches the pattern
scenarios.then: the guard MUST deny the post AND the denial MUST be logged

scenarios.name: Clean payload
scenarios.given: the HIPAA profile is enforced with the same profile.json
scenarios.when: the session posts a PR comment that matches no pattern and names no PHI-tagged path
scenarios.then: the guard MUST allow the post

requirements.text: While the HIPAA profile is enforced (the default unless the project opts out), the plugin MUST require a BAA reference for each external system that the profile lets receive data, and MUST report the profile as not ready when one is missing.

scenarios.name: BAA recorded
scenarios.given: profile.json lists a BAA reference for the model provider
scenarios.then: the check MUST report ready

scenarios.name: BAA missing
scenarios.given: profile.json lists an external system with no BAA reference
scenarios.then: the check MUST report not ready AND the outbound guard MUST deny calls to that system

requirements.text: The plugin MUST keep a control register in which each control maps to at least one OWASP Agentic AI Top 10 item (ASI01 to ASI10) or to not applicable with a reason.

scenarios.name: Complete register
scenarios.given: each control has an ASI id or a reasoned not applicable
scenarios.then: the check MUST pass

scenarios.name: Unmapped control
scenarios.given: a control has neither an ASI id nor a reasoned not applicable
scenarios.then: the check MUST fail and name the control

requirements.text: The control register MUST map each control to one NIST AI RMF function (GOVERN, MEASURE, or MANAGE), an owner role, and a review cadence with an escalation path. The default cadence is quarterly (estimate).

scenarios.name: Control with owner
scenarios.given: a control lists function MANAGE, owner role security lead, cadence quarterly
scenarios.then: the check MUST pass

scenarios.name: Missing owner
scenarios.given: a control lists no owner role
scenarios.then: the check MUST fail and name the control

requirements.text: A severity policy MUST define CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, and LOW for this repo, with examples and confidence levels, and MUST be approved by the user in DECISIONS.md before any rule blocks on severity. The policy basis is settled: four levels aligned to OWASP risk rating or CVSS bands with repo-specific examples, a per-finding confidence of High, Medium, or Low, and a SARIF mapping of CRITICAL and HIGH to error, MEDIUM to warning, LOW to note. The user approved the concrete policy text, severity-policy.md version draft-1 (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30: Severity policy approved); a rule may block on severity only after the FR-238 advisory baseline.

scenarios.name: Policy approved
scenarios.given: the policy exists and a DECISIONS.md entry approves it
scenarios.when: a rule is switched to blocking
scenarios.then: the switch MUST succeed

scenarios.name: Policy missing
scenarios.given: no approved policy exists
scenarios.when: a rule is switched to blocking
scenarios.then: the switch MUST be refused with the missing-policy reason

requirements.text: Each new check that can block MUST run advisory-only first, record every finding, and produce a baseline report with finding counts and precision before promotion to blocking. The baseline lasts 14 days or 20 reviews, whichever is later (estimate, BRD A-5).

scenarios.name: Advisory run
scenarios.given: a check is in advisory mode
scenarios.then: it MUST record the finding AND it MUST NOT block

scenarios.name: Promotion without baseline
scenarios.given: a check has no baseline report
scenarios.then: the switch MUST be refused

requirements.text: A finding MUST route as blocking only when confidence is high and severity is HIGH or CRITICAL under the severity policy; every other finding MUST route as advisory.

scenarios.name: Critical, high confidence
scenarios.given: a finding with severity CRITICAL and confidence high
scenarios.then: the finding MUST route as block-merge

scenarios.name: High severity, low confidence
scenarios.given: a finding with severity HIGH and confidence low
scenarios.then: the finding MUST route as inline-comment or log-only AND it MUST NOT block merge

requirements.text: The reviewer and code-reviewer agents MUST give each finding a severity, a confidence, and a routing field with one of block-merge, inline-comment, or log-only.

scenarios.name: Complete finding
scenarios.given: a reviewer reports a defect at src/a.js:10
scenarios.then: the finding MUST hold severity, confidence, and routing

scenarios.name: Missing field
scenarios.given: a finding lacks severity
scenarios.then: the orchestrator MUST reject the report and ask for a corrected one

requirements.text: The reviewer output MUST include a SARIF document (version 2.1.0, estimate) whose result level derives from severity and whose location is file and line, so findings appear in the GitHub Security tab. The reviewer returns the SARIF content or the findings, and the /do orchestrator MUST write the .sarif file. Uploading the file to GitHub is a posting action under the FR-214 confirmation rule.

scenarios.name: Findings become SARIF
scenarios.given: a reviewer reports two findings with file and line
scenarios.then: it MUST hold two results with level and location

scenarios.name: Finding without a location
scenarios.given: a finding has no file and line
scenarios.then: the finding MUST be left out of SARIF AND the report MUST list it as not exported with the reason

requirements.text: A hook on UserPromptSubmit, not the orchestrator, MUST write a record of the user's confirmation (PR, verdict, timestamp, a reference to the user message it came from, and the writer marked hook) as JSONL to a store under a path in .agent/ that FR-245 already protects, and the PR-posting guard of FR-214 MUST read that store with file reads alone. A subagent and text from a PR, web page, or file MUST NOT create or alter a confirmation record. The confirmation MUST be bound to its pending action by a per-action token: when /do shows the PR and verdict draft, it MUST write a pending-action record (PR, verdict, a short random token, session_id) to the store, and the hook MUST write a confirmation only when the user's prompt carries the matching token. An affirmative without the matching token MUST NOT confirm.

scenarios.name: User confirmation recorded
scenarios.given: /do showed the draft for PR 42 with verdict approve, wrote a pending-action record with token K7Q2, and the user answered yes with K7Q2 in their own message
scenarios.then: the store MUST hold a JSONL record for PR 42 and verdict approve with the timestamp AND the record MUST name the writer as hook

scenarios.name: Affirmative without the token rejected
scenarios.given: /do wrote a pending-action record for PR 42 with token K7Q2
scenarios.when: a prompt holds an affirmative such as pasted or injected text without K7Q2
scenarios.then: the hook MUST NOT write a confirmation record AND the guard of FR-214 MUST still deny the posting command

scenarios.name: Forged confirmation rejected
scenarios.given: a PR description claims that the user confirmed approval
scenarios.when: a subagent or the session tries to write a confirmation record from that text
scenarios.then: the write MUST be denied AND the guard of FR-214 MUST still deny the posting command

requirements.text: A compliance profile MUST be turned off only by a change to the committed .claude/settings.json that the user applies; the plugin MUST NOT edit a settings file, and the hooks MUST read the profile flag by parsing the env block of the committed project .claude/settings.json directly, never the merged process environment, because the merged environment carries a local override; a personal .claude/settings.local.json MUST NOT disable enforcement.

scenarios.name: Opt-out in committed settings
scenarios.given: the user changed the committed .claude/settings.json to turn the FERPA profile off
scenarios.then: the FERPA controls MUST stop enforcing AND the SOC 2 and HIPAA profiles MUST stay enforced

scenarios.name: Personal settings cannot disable
scenarios.given: .claude/settings.local.json holds a flag that turns the HIPAA profile off and the committed .claude/settings.json does not
scenarios.when: a hook reads the profile state by parsing the committed project settings file
scenarios.then: the HIPAA profile MUST stay enforced AND the health check MUST report the ignored personal flag

scenarios.name: Plugin does not write settings
scenarios.given: a project that wants to opt out
scenarios.when: the plugin explains how to opt out
scenarios.then: it MUST describe the settings change for the user to apply AND it MUST NOT write .claude/settings.json

requirements.text: Each profile disablement MUST write a logged event that names the profile and the time, and MUST have its own DECISIONS.md entry.

scenarios.name: Disablement logged
scenarios.given: the committed settings turn the HIPAA profile off
scenarios.then: the audit log MUST hold a disablement event naming the HIPAA profile and the time

scenarios.name: No decision entry
scenarios.given: a profile is off and DECISIONS.md holds no entry for that disablement
scenarios.then: the report MUST list the disablement as lacking a decision entry

requirements.text: These six paths MUST be protected from writes by every subagent: .claude/settings.json, .agent/governance/profile.json, the confirmation store of FR-242, .agent/logs/governance/**, the session purpose record of FR-247, and the rule-mode store (the store that holds the advisory or blocking mode of each check, FR-238). A hook or the orchestrator remains the only writer of the last four. The FR-246 attribution decision adds no new store and no seventh path: the six protected paths are unchanged, and .agent/governance/profile.json (path 2) is the trust anchor for the FR-246 receiving-party allowlist.

scenarios.name: Subagent write denied
scenarios.given: a subagent session
scenarios.then: the write bar MUST deny the write AND the log MUST hold a deny record

scenarios.name: Evidence and toggle stores denied
scenarios.given: a subagent session
scenarios.when: it writes the confirmation store, a file under .agent/logs/governance/, the session purpose record, or the rule-mode store
scenarios.then: the write bar MUST deny the write AND the log MUST hold a deny record

scenarios.name: Read allowed
scenarios.given: a subagent session
scenarios.then: the read MUST be allowed

requirements.text: While the FERPA profile is enforced (the default unless the project opts out), the plugin MUST log each disclosure of education-record data to an outside party, recording the receiving party and the legitimate interest for each. The log MUST NOT accept unstated for either field; when the receiving party or the legitimate interest is missing, the plugin MUST deny the outbound call. The receiving party and the legitimate interest MUST be declared in the outbound call payload, and the guard (a read-only PreToolUse hook) MUST parse them from that payload. The guard MUST validate the receiving party against an allowlist held in .agent/governance/profile.json, and MUST deny the call when the receiving party is not on that allowlist. The control MUST apply the exceptions of 34 CFR 99.32(d), so a disclosure covered by an exception does not need a recorded entry under this control. Outbound disclosure detection is imperfect: a paraphrase or a payload assembled from earlier reads can escape a pattern or path match.

scenarios.name: Disclosure recorded
scenarios.given: the FERPA profile is enforced and an outbound call names a student-record path, with a receiving party and a legitimate interest declared
scenarios.then: the audit log MUST hold the receiving party and the legitimate interest for that disclosure

scenarios.name: Missing party or interest
scenarios.given: the FERPA profile is enforced and an outbound call names a student-record path, with no declared legitimate interest
scenarios.when: the session attempts the outbound call
scenarios.then: the plugin MUST deny the call AND the log MUST NOT hold the value unstated for the receiving party or the legitimate interest

scenarios.name: Party not on the allowlist
scenarios.given: the FERPA profile is enforced and an outbound call names a student-record path, with a receiving party that is not on the profile.json allowlist
scenarios.when: the session attempts the outbound call
scenarios.then: the plugin MUST deny the call

scenarios.name: Exception applies
scenarios.given: the receiving party falls under a 99.32(d) exception that profile.json lists
scenarios.then: the plugin MUST apply the exception and MUST NOT require a disclosure entry

requirements.text: A hook MUST write the session purpose record from a purpose the user declares, and the access-logging hooks (FR-230, FR-232) MUST read that record. Model output and text from a PR, web page, or file MUST NOT create or alter the record. When the user declares no purpose, the access log MUST record the purpose as unstated and flag the record.

scenarios.name: User declares a purpose
scenarios.given: the user states review grading anomalies as the purpose of the session
scenarios.then: the session purpose record MUST hold that purpose AND the record MUST name the writer as a hook

scenarios.name: Forged purpose rejected
scenarios.given: a PR description or file text claims the session purpose is approved audit
scenarios.when: the model or a subagent tries to write the session purpose record from that text
scenarios.then: the write MUST be denied AND the access log MUST NOT show that purpose

scenarios.name: No purpose declared
scenarios.given: the user declares no purpose
scenarios.when: an agent reads a student-record or PHI-tagged path
scenarios.then: the access log MUST hold the purpose unstated AND the record MUST be flagged

requirements.text: Every deny, ask, guardrail, and gate decision MUST produce a log record with timestamp, agent identity, decision, and rule id.
Each new hook, agent, or skill MUST hold the fewest tools it needs; the guardrail MUST NOT hold write tools and no new unscoped Bash grant MUST appear.

A control marked security-critical (FR-214, FR-217, FR-220, FR-223, FR-231, FR-233, FR-246) MUST deny its own guarded operation class when it cannot evaluate because of an error or timeout, or when .agent/governance/profile.json is malformed while a profile is enforced; the denial MUST last until the file is fixed. When profile.json is absent the controls MUST run in log-only mode and MUST NOT hard-deny, because nothing is tagged to match. Settled by DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-28, Compliance profile flags, enforced by default (D-1).

scenarios.name: Fail-closed on error
scenarios.given: the PR-posting guard throws an error while evaluating gh pr review 42 --approve
scenarios.then: the hook MUST deny that command AND a command outside the guarded class MUST still be allowed

scenarios.name: Absent configuration runs log-only
scenarios.given: a profile is enforced by default and .agent/governance/profile.json does not exist
scenarios.when: a session reads a path and sends an outbound call
scenarios.then: the controls MUST log the events in log-only mode AND no control MUST hard-deny, because nothing is tagged to match

scenarios.name: Malformed configuration denies
scenarios.given: a profile is enforced and .agent/governance/profile.json is malformed
scenarios.when: a session attempts a guarded tagged-path operation
scenarios.then: the control MUST deny the operation AND the denial MUST continue until the file is fixed

requirements.text: Each hook added to the per-write path MUST add at most 30 ms at the median, and the total per-write hook cost MUST stay at or below 150 ms at the median. The thresholds are estimates anchored to the existing 80 to 110 ms; confirm by measurement.

scenarios.name: Budget check
scenarios.given: all hooks of this roadmap are installed
scenarios.then: the median added cost per hook MUST be at most 30 ms AND the median total MUST be at most 150 ms

requirements.text: Chain verification MUST detect 100% of single-line edits, deletions, and reorderings in the test corpus and MUST finish a 100,000-line log in at most 10 seconds (estimate for the time limit).

scenarios.name: Tamper detection
scenarios.given: a test corpus with one edited, one deleted, and one reordered line
scenarios.then: all three MUST be detected

requirements.text: Logs MUST NOT hold prompt text, file contents, or secret values; the data-accessed field MUST hold a path and a data-class tag only.

scenarios.name: Secret value kept out of the log
scenarios.given: the secret scan finds an API key in a staged file
scenarios.then: the record MUST hold the path and rule name AND the record MUST NOT hold the key value

requirements.text: Audit and subagent logs MUST rotate by size, each new segment MUST carry the prior segment's final chain hash so the hash chain verifies across the cut, and segments MUST be retained for at least 12 months. The rotation size is an estimate until measured against NFR-030.

scenarios.name: Rotation keeps the chain
scenarios.given: the log reaches its configured rotation size (an estimate until measured)
scenarios.then: the first line of the new segment MUST hold the hash of the last line of the old segment AND chain verification MUST pass across the cut

requirements.text: A compliance control that rests on a vendor blog or an unverified citation MUST be labeled directional, and a control MUST NOT be marked complete before verification against the regulation text. Status: the HIPAA audit control (FR-232) is verified against 45 CFR 164.312(b), which requires mechanisms that record and examine activity, and the control implements that one required technical safeguard, not full HIPAA compliance. The FERPA internal access log (FR-230) carries no 34 CFR 99.32 citation and is general governance support, labeled directional. The FERPA disclosure-recordation control (FR-246) is the only control cited against 34 CFR 99.32; it stays to verify until its exception handling is reviewed. The exact log rotation size of NFR-032 is an estimate until measured against the NFR-030 verification-time target. The severity-policy basis (FR-237) is settled and the user approved the concrete policy text, severity-policy.md version draft-1 (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30: Severity policy approved); a rule may block on severity only after the FR-238 advisory baseline. The figures "under 50% mitigation" and "18% governance councils" MUST NOT serve as a threshold.

scenarios.name: Unverified FERPA disclosure control
scenarios.given: the FERPA disclosure-recordation control (FR-246) has no verification note
scenarios.then: the control status MUST read to verify and not complete

scenarios.name: FERPA internal log not cited as 99.32
scenarios.given: the FERPA internal access log (FR-230) sits in the control register
scenarios.then: the entry MUST NOT cite 34 CFR 99.32 and MUST read as general governance support

scenarios.name: HIPAA control states its scope
scenarios.given: the HIPAA audit control (FR-232) is marked verified
scenarios.then: the entry MUST cite 45 CFR 164.312(b) as one safeguard AND the entry MUST NOT claim full HIPAA compliance

requirements.text: A rule MUST NOT move from advisory to blocking unless its baseline precision is at least 90% (estimate, BRD A-6).

scenarios.name: Low-precision promotion
scenarios.given: a baseline precision of 70%
scenarios.when: the rule is switched to blocking
scenarios.then: the switch MUST be refused with the precision value

requirements.text: Each new guard or filter MUST ship a self-test corpus with a known-safe and a known-prohibited case, report through the health check, and pass the table sync checks.
Every change to the LLM surface made for this roadmap MUST carry LLM Security Clear before merge, and any write-guard narrowing MUST follow a DECISIONS.md entry.

traceability.verified_by: hook self-test and acceptance test: PR verdict deny
commit skill acceptance test with a seeded secret
review-protocol document review and loop test
gate record inspection in an acceptance test
unit test of the log writer
confirmation store write-bar test and guard acceptance test
settings source acceptance test and health check self-test
disablement log record inspection and health check
write-bar self-test covering all six protected paths
outbound disclosure guard self-test and FERPA profile acceptance test
purpose-capture hook self-test and access log inspection
tamper test corpus and timing run

out_of_scope.item: Gaps 5, 7, 8, 9 of the LLM security checklist
Cryptographic signing of the audit log with an external key
out_of_scope.reason: The roadmap asks for a hash chain only

out_of_scope.item: Content-level PHI detection beyond configured patterns and tagged paths
out_of_scope.reason: No accepted method for paraphrase detection

out_of_scope.item: Session-level taint tracking that denies a payload holding content earlier read from a PHI-tagged path or student-record path (FR-233, FR-246)
out_of_scope.reason: A per-call hook has no session state; no tracking mechanism is named

out_of_scope.item: Bash write coverage through symlinks and variable-built commands
out_of_scope.reason: Existing known limit of the write bar

out_of_scope.item: Vendor SOC 2 report, HIPAA attestation, or FERPA certification for the plugin
out_of_scope.reason: Evidence comes from the plugin's own hooks; certification is the adopter's process
Findings go to the GitHub Security tab, not a separate dashboard

open_questions: OQ-1: Resolved (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30, Judgement-gate evidence and the /do human authorizer settled). A judgement-based gate clears on a scanner exit code from the plugin's own scripts plus a distinct reviewer-agent verdict with file:line findings; an external scanner is optional additional evidence (FR-221).

OQ-2: Resolved (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30, Gap-3 push grant and gap-6 revision-loop cap settled). The cap is 10 with two consecutive LGTMs as the normal pass; at the cap the orchestrator escalates with continue, waive, or abort (FR-218).

OQ-3: Resolved (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30, Audit-logging stores settled (per-access split, rotation and retention, confirmation-store writer)). Size-based rotation replaces the 500-line cap, carries the prior segment's final chain hash into each new segment, and keeps segments at least 12 months; the rotation size is an estimate (NFR-032).
OQ-4: Resolved (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30, Audit-logging stores settled (per-access split, rotation and retention, confirmation-store writer)). The two-file split of FR-227 is ratified as written.

OQ-5: Settled. Security-critical controls may fail closed on a malformed configuration while a profile is enforced; an absent configuration runs log-only (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-28, Compliance profile flags, enforced by default).

OQ-6: Settled. An access to a tagged path with no recorded purpose is logged unstated and flagged, never denied on the missing purpose alone (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-28, FERPA/HIPAA purpose capture, missing-purpose handling, and governance path protection; FR-230).

OQ-7: Resolved (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30, Judgement-gate evidence and the /do human authorizer settled). The authorizer is the user who approved the plan, recorded as a reference to that approval and never message text; an autonomous or unapproved action records none with a reason (FR-227).

OQ-8: Resolved (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30, Severity-policy basis and SARIF writer settled). The /do orchestrator writes the SARIF file; the reviewer stays read-only; uploading to GitHub falls under the FR-214 confirmation rule (FR-241).

OQ-9: Resolved (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-28, OQ-9 resolved; FERPA control reframed, HIPAA scope tightened). HIPAA: FR-232 is verified against 45 CFR 164.312(b) as one required technical safeguard that records and supports review, not full HIPAA compliance. FERPA: the internal access log (FR-230) is general governance support and does not implement 34 CFR 99.32; FR-246 adds disclosure recordation for outbound education-record data and is the only control cited against 99.32.

OQ-10: Resolved (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30, Audit-logging stores settled (per-access split, rotation and retention, confirmation-store writer)). A UserPromptSubmit hook writes the confirmation store as JSONL under a path in .agent/ protected under FR-245; the FR-214 guard reads it with file reads alone (FR-242).

OQ-11: Resolved. A hook writes the session purpose record from a purpose the user declares, and the access-logging hooks read it; with no declared purpose the log records unstated and flags the record (FR-247).

OQ-12: Resolved (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30: Severity policy approved). The user approved severity-policy.md version draft-1. The policy basis was settled earlier (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-30, Severity-policy basis and SARIF writer settled); a rule may block on severity only after the FR-238 advisory baseline (FR-237).
